reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about entropy-driven stabilization, diffusion suppression, and comparative behavior, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge covers configurational entropy in bulk alloys, but the extension to nanoalloys and the specific mechanistic claims require supporting citations which are absent.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes a single-phase, disordered atomic arrangement in high-entropy nanoalloys
This single-phase structure minimizes phase separation and grain growth
The mechanism involves reduced atomic diffusion due to high mixing entropy and lattice distortions
Low-entropy (binary/ternary) nanoalloys are more prone to phase transformation and grain coarsening under the same conditions
